svg.title: Architecture diagram
svg.desc: From left to right: the external side (iOS app, Entra ID, administrators, Akamai, Netskope, APNs); the iDMZ account (API Gateway REST with its authorizer, and the web ALB); the platform account in us-east-1 with the services VPC (internal NLB, web app, panel, Admin API, the api backend, which creates and launches runs, and three Lambdas, each in its own box: the watchdog, which finds dead runs every minute, the daily chat expiry, which calls deleteChat, and the chat deletion Lambda, which reads the chat deletion queue, stops the chat's microVM and deletes S3, messages, COST# and the chat, all three writing to DynamoDB; two more Lambdas, each in its own box, drawn next to DynamoDB, in the lower part of the same VPC frame: the run events Lambda, which reads the DynamoDB stream, closes with close(run_id) when it sees end, copies pending approvals and memory proposals into CTL# and notifies the backend of ends and pending approvals, and the cost Lambda, which receives the Bedrock invocation log from CloudWatch Logs and writes the spend, the budget denial and the alerts), DynamoDB (four tables: activity, configuration, OBO and audit), the standard SQS task queue (Scheduler drops the firings and the backend reads them and launches them as a chat) and the chat deletion queue (deleteChat drops the chat, from the backend or the chat expiry Lambda, and the chat deletion Lambda deletes it), the agents VPC with the kernel on AgentCore Runtime V2, one microVM per chat, which calls Bedrock directly, and next to it the MCP integrations VPC with the MCP Hub, mcp-documents, mcp-time and other MCPs connected to the corporate network, and the regional services (SQS, EventBridge Scheduler, KMS, CloudWatch, Secrets Manager, S3, Bedrock and Knowledge Bases); at the bottom, the AgentCore managed service (Evaluations). The hub reads and marks approvals in DynamoDB (not drawn). The chat deletion queue has no arrows (deleteChat fills it and the chat deletion Lambda consumes it), like the hub's approvals.
svg.text: Services VPC · no IGW · VPC endpoints
Agents VPC · no routes · DNS Firewall
MCP integrations VPC · → corporate network (TGW / DX / VPN)
1 microVM per chat · no user token
events and usage → DynamoDB · chat workspace ↔ S3
code: local (shell), in the microVM itself
search_documents · mandatory agent and group filters
in-house or third-party → corporate network APIs
deleteChat (api, chat expiry) → chat deletion Lambda
reads the kernel's OTEL traces in CloudWatch · online: % of real sessions
batch from the panel before publishing a version · scores per agent and version
